extracted.intended_audience: researchers and clinicians conducting inter-rater reliability, instrument validation, and measurement studies (healthcare/clinical research)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, metrics, and empirical examples for assessing inter-rater and intra-rater reliability of clinical/observational measurement instruments (e.g., rating scales, triage systems, chart abstraction). Includes statistical measures, feasibility criteria, and procedural recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's kappa (including 95% CI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cohen's kappa to estimate intra- and inter-rater reliability for categorical items; often reported with 95% confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples across studies: kappa values reported across ranges (e.g., 0.22–0.90). Studies report kappa for pain provocation, mobility, end-feel, tear presence/thickness, diagnosis concordance, etc. Report kappa alongside percent agreement and interpret using conventional descriptors (fair/moderate/substantial/almost perfect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage agreement (raw, positive and negative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report percent agreement (overall or split into positive/negative agreement) between raters as a simple descriptive measure of concordance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several studies reported percentage agreements (e.g., 61%–90%, 78%). Use percent agreement together with chance-corrected statistics (kappa) because raw agreement is not chance-adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to estimate overall agreement for ordinal or continuous measures and for sumscores (e.g., mean scale scores, total scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ICCs reported as 0.86, 0.97, 0.65, etc. Use ICC for continuous/ordinal aggregated scores and report interpretation (e.g., >0.75 often described as excellent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted kappa (quadratic/other) for ordinal items
rubrics_metrics.description: Use weighted kappa (e.g., quadratic weight) when items are ordinal so that partial agreement is accounted for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as 'Cohen's quadratic weighted kappa' or 'weighted kappa' in studies of classification levels and note scoring (examples: кw >0.90 intra-rater, кw >0.85 inter-rater).

rubrics_metrics.name: AC1 statistic (Gwet's AC1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report AC1 as an alternative or supplement to kappa to address prevalence-related issues in agreement estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside kappa in some studies to show 'very high agreement' when kappa may be affected by trait prevalence (examples: AC1 = .83, risk assessment AC1 = .94).

rubrics_metrics.name: Krippendorff's alpha
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Krippendorff's alpha for inter-rater reliability assessment, particularly with multiple raters or varied data types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as one of the reliability metrics calculated for instrument assessment (used alongside kappa, ICC, percent agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: McNemar's test of symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply McNemar's test to test symmetry for paired categorical item responses as a measure of item-level reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in questionnaire/scale reliability studies to examine item reliability in paired-assessment designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test-retest reliability / intra-rater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess stability of the same rater's scores across repeated assessments (test-retest or intrarater reliability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: retest intervals varied (e.g., ~70 days, ~2 weeks). Report intrarater kappa/ICC and compare with inter-rater reliability to assess consistency over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity, specificity, and AUC for validity/predictive ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sensitivity, specificity, and area under the ROC curve (AUC) to assess predictive validity of classification/triage systems against outcomes (e.g., admission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ESI predicted admission with sensitivity 52%, specificity 81%, AUC 0.78. Use these measures to complement reliability stats when evaluating a tool's appropriateness for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizability (G) studies to examine variance components
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct generalizability analyses to decompose score variance into components (cases, raters, case-by-task interactions) and to estimate overall reliability across design choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: substantial variance from case specificity and case-task specificity; rater-associated variance often modest (<5%). Use G-studies to inform number of cases and raters needed for acceptable reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training and calibration with case- and level-specific scoring guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide rater training and case/level-specific scoring guidelines to improve rater calibration and scoring consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raters reported that having such guidelines during training was most helpful; justification/scoring was often cited as the hardest to score without detailed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility metrics: clarity, ease, and completion time
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate feasibility of instruments by measuring clarity (rater perception), ease-of-use, and time to complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ICU Mobility Scale participants reported clarity and 95% noted it took <1 minute to complete. Feasibility data support instrument adoption in clinical workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus/composite expert review as operational gold standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Use consensus or composite review by expert clinicians as an operational gold standard against which individual rater classifications are compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: composite review by two shoulder specialists used as the operational gold standard for MRI reading; used to compute sensitivity/specificity of other raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report prevalence index and bias index when using kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate and report prevalence index and bias index to aid interpretation of kappa values affected by trait prevalence and rater bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some studies explicitly calculated prevalence and bias indices along with kappa because kappa can be misleading when prevalence is very low or very high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple complementary statistical measures rather than a single metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Report a suite of agreement statistics (e.g., kappa, percent agreement, ICC, AC1, Krippendorff's alpha) to provide a fuller picture of reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most studies reported several metrics; different metrics are appropriate for different data types and reliability aspects (item vs overall score, categorical vs continuous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument content development via expert panel or Delphi procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop instrument content and items using structured expert consensus methods (e.g., expert panel discussion, written Delphi) to ensure content validity before reliability testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: EFIP content determined using a written Delphi procedure; BFMF2 content discussed by an expert panel and revised to include explanatory figures and precise descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve data definitions, abstractor training, and real-time data collection for poor-reliability variables
rubrics_metrics.description: When certain variables (often time-related events) show poor reliability, recommend improving variable definitions, abstractor training, and implementing real-time data capture systems (especially in ED settings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: PCNASR study recommended specific actions for variables with poor kappa (stroke onset time, time of initial imaging, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize number of raters and cases to balance reliability and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Design scoring/assessment protocols to balance the number of raters and cases in order to maximize reliability given limited resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: patient note scoring designs may optimize reliability by adjusting numbers of raters vs cases; G-study results can inform this balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable classification from short video recordings using precise figures/descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear figures and precise level descriptions so raters can determine classification levels from short video recordings (feasible and useful for research/clinical practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: BFMF2 classification levels could be determined from <5 minute video recordings using included figures and precise descriptions, supporting feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation thresholds and descriptive labels for agreement statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply conventional descriptive labels (e.g., poor/fair/moderate/substantial/almost perfect or acceptable/excellent) to kappa/ICC values to aid interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies used labels such as 'fair', 'moderate', 'substantial', 'almost perfect' and sometimes 'excellent' for ICC >0.75; explicitly state thresholds used and report confidence intervals to contextualize point estimates.
